**Allowed origins** are decided by the `origin` function passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts`, at lines 19–31. It's applied globally with `app.use('*', cors(...))`. A request origin is echoed back, and so allowed, only if it is one of these:
- exactly `http://localhost:4200`
- anything ending in `.pages.dev`, at any depth
- anything ending in `.workers.dev`, at any depth

An empty origin returns `null`, and so does any other origin, so no CORS headers are sent for them. The allowed methods are `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` and `OPTIONS`.

**To add a custom domain**, edit that same function in `worker/src/index.ts`. Add another condition to the `if (...)` at lines 23–27, for example:
- `origin === 'https://play.example.com'` for an exact match, or
- `origin.endsWith('.example.com')` for subdomains.

Use a full origin string, including the scheme (`https://`) and any port. Don't put wildcards in an array. Hono matches array entries as exact strings, which is why the code uses a function. The `.endsWith()` checks are loose. `.endsWith('.example.com')` matches any subdomain, so only use it for domains you control.

You don't need to change `worker/wrangler.toml` for CORS. It only declares the bindings (`AI`, `SESSION_KV`, `DB`, `ENVIRONMENT`). Redeploy the Worker after the edit. `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 covers CORS in more detail, though I didn't read it.
